pr_title: soc: nrf: basic power management for nrf53 and nrf91
pr_body:
Only System OFF mode is supported. Based on nrf52 power management, but nrf53 and nrf91 use nrf_regulators HAL instead of nrf_power.

Fixes #21318
pr_comments:
**All checks passed.**



*Tip: The bot edits this comment instead of posting a new one, so you can check the comment's history to see earlier messages.*

@masz-nordic If it is true that the nrf_regulator is only available for the application core then the current changes need another modification. We need to move the `select HAS_SYS_POWER_STATE_DEEP_SLEEP_1` from Kconfig.soc to the Application core Kconfig seeing as the following code in power.c includes the regulator for both cores at the moment:
```
#ifdef CONFIG_HAS_SYS_POWER_STATE_DEEP_SLEEP_1
#include <hal/nrf_regulators.h>
#endif
```

**EDIT**
I just realized that this definition of "deep sleep" relies on the nrf_regulators.h implementation and therefore the code needs no more modification. I simply misunderstood what was happening. Is there not another way to put the network core into SYSTEM_OFF sleep mode?

**EDIT 2**
It appears that the nrf5340 supports a "Core Force-off mode" in which the app core can force the network core off. This is likely the scope of another commit.

@MarcianoPreciado 
> We need to move the select HAS_SYS_POWER_STATE_DEEP_SLEEP_1 from Kconfig.soc to the Application core Kconfig

That is a part of this PR, see changes in nRF53 `Kconfig.series` and `Kconfig.soc`.

>It appears that the nrf5340 supports a "Core Force-off mode" in which the app core can force the network core off. This is likely the scope of another commit.

Correct, this is just basic power management, similar to nRF52. Controlling the network core from application core (see also https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/boards/arm/nrf5340_dk_nrf5340/nrf5340_cpunet_reset.c) should be done in a separate PR.
Any update on this PR? @masz-nordic did you see the latest feedback from @pabigot? @ioannisg have you had a look at this PR?
Overall, I think `power.c` needs to be a common file for nrf SoCs, as @pabigot suggested

issue_context.title: CONFIG_SYS_POWER_MANAGEMENT Makes Build Fail for nRF5340 and nRF9160
issue_context.body:
The current implementation of `zephyr/subsys/power/device.c` breaks because of the following:

```
#if defined(CONFIG_SYS_POWER_MANAGEMENT)
...
/*
 * FIXME: Remove the conditional inclusion of
 * core_devices array once we enble the capability
 * to build the device list based on devices power
 * and clock domain dependencies.
 */
#if defined(CONFIG_SOC_SERIES_NRF52X) || defined(CONFIG_SOC_SERIES_NRF51X)
#define MAX_PM_DEVICES	15
#define NUM_CORE_DEVICES	4
#define MAX_DEV_NAME_LEN	16
static const char core_devices[NUM_CORE_DEVICES][MAX_DEV_NAME_LEN] = {
	"CLOCK_32K",
	"CLOCK_16M",
	"sys_clock",
	"UART_0",
};
#else
#error "Add SoC's core devices list for PM"
#endif
...
#endif /* defined(CONFIG_SYS_POWER_MANAGEMENT) */
```
The documentation describes that `SYS_POWER_MANAGEMENT` is dependent on `SOC_FAMILY_NRF` which is selected by `SOC_SERIES_NRF51X`, `SOC_SERIES_NRF52X`, `SOC_SERIES_NRF53X`, `SOC_SERIES_NRF91X`. Both of the soc_series symbols for the nRF53x and nRF91x select `HAS_SYS_POWER_STATE_DEEP_SLEEP_1` also which shows that the system power management functionality was intended to be compatible for both series.

I'm currently working on an extreme low-power iot device on the nRF5340 and this feature is necessary to reach the lowest power state without losing significant development time. I'd be happy to help via a pull request, but I am quite new to Zephyr and am not yet familiar enough to start modifying the codebase.
comments: @MarcianoPreciado can you try #21075 and see if it helps?
@masz-nordic I tried the pull request you mentioned and it seems to help a lot! Do you know exactly what is holding it up from being merged?
I will close the issue once your pull request is accepted.

review_comments: This file is identical to the one added for nrf53, except that this one doesn't conditionalize the include on `CONFIG_HAS_SYS_POWER_STATE_DEEP_SLEEP_1`.  It's also remarkably similar to nrf51 and nrf52, differing only in the include file and the spelling of `power_system_off`.  Could it perhaps be moved to a `soc/arm/nordic_nrf/common` directory to reduce the need to make changes in four files as the power management infrastructure starts to mature?

Those files are almost identical now, but I have created separate ones to prepare for potential differences in power management's future implementation. As for now, they could be merged into one, I don't have a strong opinion on this.
I don't believe we generally indent preprocessor directives.
I left it like this to keep conistent with `nrf52/power.c`. Should I delete indents here and in `nrf52`?

No, let's leave that for some future progress toward #21392.  I'd rather have less noise with internal consistency, than partial steps toward project-wide consistency.  (There are 570 indented `#if*` statements in Zephyr, compared to 15289 that are not.)
We should not indent preprocessor directives, that's true
